venue.name: The Raptors
venue.description: The Raptors is a birds of prey centre on Herd Road just north of Duncan, and the footer of its own site says it is also known as Pacific Northwest Raptors Ltd. Visitors walk the grounds to see eagles, hawks, owls and vultures, and flying demonstrations are included with admission. The hands on experiences, the Hawk Walk and the Encounter, start at age eight, and the gift shop can arrange a shorter Kids Encounter for four to seven year olds. School and community groups can book a field trip with a guided tour and a flying demonstration, or have staff bring three birds to the school instead.

facility_notes.lunch_space: We do offer some light snacks in our gift shop, but the centre does not have any meal options. You are more than welcome to bring your own food to the centre and enjoy it at one of our picnic benches.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: All common personal belongings are permitted, including coolers, backpacks, strollers, wagons, outside food and drink (with the exception of alcohol) and cameras.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Our facility is wheelchair accessible, as long as your personal mobility aids are equipped to deal with outdoor surfaces. While some of our paths are paved, the majority are hard-packed earth or packed gravel.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Parking is free of charge. During the summer months, the parking lot can get busy so we strongly recommend carpooling whenever possible.

restrictions: For the comfort and safety of our birds dogs are not permitted in the facility. Guests with service animals, please contact us to arrange accomodations.
All guests must wear a shirt and shoes at all time.
You must be eight years or older to participate in our CLOSER or CLOSEST admission packages, or any other hands-on experience.
Outside food and drink are permitted with the exception of alcohol.
venue.hours_notes: Summer hours run from 1 July to 6 September, open every day 10:00 to 17:00, with flying demonstrations at 11:00, 13:30 and 16:00. From 8 to 29 September the centre is open every day 12:00 to 15:00 with one demonstration at 13:30, and it is closed on 7 September. From 1 October to 2 November it is open 12:00 to 15:00 Tuesday to Sunday, closed Mondays, with one demonstration at 13:30.
venue.seasonal_notes: The hours published on the site stop at 2 November and nothing is shown for the winter. The Owl Encounter is listed as unavailable and returning in November 2026.

programs.name: Field Trips
programs.description: A visit to the centre for a class or group. It includes a 20 to 30 minute guided tour of the facility and a flying demonstration. No price is published for groups; the page says to contact them for pricing and to book.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the paths with a guide past the aviaries to look at the many bird species kept there, then watch a flying demonstration where eagles, hawks, owls and vultures fly overhead.
programs.our_note: There is no price anywhere on the site for a group, so cost is the first thing to settle on the phone. Most of the visit is outside on packed earth or gravel, and there is no meal to buy on site, so send lunches and dress the children for the weather.
programs.practical_summary: There are picnic benches for a packed lunch and parking is free. Washrooms, shelter if it rains and room for a bus are not mentioned anywhere on the site, so ask when you call.
programs.evidence: Learn about our facility while enjoying a 20-30 minute guided tour

programs.name: School & Community Visits
programs.description: Staff bring birds to a school, community group or event. Each presentation is a 30 minute talk with three different birds, with extra time for questions and discussion. Birds will not be flying at away locations without prior planning. No price is published; the page says to contact them for pricing and to book.
programs.what_children_do: Meet three different birds one at a time as an educator holds each one and talks about it, then ask questions at the end.
programs.our_note: The birds stay on the glove unless flying has been arranged in advance, so say up front if you want the children to see one fly. Nothing is published about how far they travel or what it costs, so ask about both.
programs.practical_summary: They come to you, so the washrooms, lunch space and indoor room are your own. Price, group size and how much notice they need are not published, so ask when you call.
programs.evidence: Each presentation consists of a 30 minute talk with 3 different birds, with additional time for questions and discussion.

programs.name: CLOSE General Admission
programs.description: All day admission to the centre with a flying demonstration included. Adults are $28, youth aged 4 to 17 are $20, children aged 0 to 3 are free, and a group of four or more gets 10 percent off. This is the published walk in rate rather than a rate written for schools. Reservations are not required, and re-entry on the same day is allowed if you get a stamp at the gift shop.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the paths past the aviaries at their own pace to look at eagles, hawks, owls and vultures, then watch a flying demonstration where the birds fly overhead and an educator talks about them.
programs.our_note: Under fours get in free, but every hands on option starts at eight, so a preschool group is looking and watching rather than holding a bird. If you want something hands on for four to seven year olds, ask at the gift shop on the day about the Kids Encounter.
programs.practical_summary: Parking is free, picnic benches are there for a packed lunch, and the only food sold is light snacks. Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site, which is worth a call before you bring a young group.
programs.extra_fees_note: A group of four or more gets a 10 percent discount. Children aged 0 to 3 are free and seniors, students and veterans are $25.
programs.evidence: Get close to some amazing predators! Tour the facility, meet our birds, and experience our featured flying demonstrations.

programs.name: Kids Encounter
programs.description: A shorter hands on option for children too young for the Hawk Walk and the Encounter, both of which start at age eight. The site says pre-booking is not required and to inquire with the gift shop. No price is published.
programs.what_children_do: Put on a glove and hold one of the smaller birds with a staff member alongside.
programs.our_note: This one is only mentioned in an answer inside the questions panel, not on a page of its own, so staff may need reminding it exists. Ask what it costs and how many children they can take through in one visit.
programs.practical_summary: It runs at the centre alongside a normal admission, so the same free parking and picnic benches apply. Price, how long it takes and how many children can do it are all unpublished.
programs.evidence: We do offer a Kids Encounter for younger guests age 4-7.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: the tracker address www.pnwraptors.com now redirects to the-raptors.com. The footer of every page says 'Also known as "Pacific Northwest Raptors Ltd."' and gives the same Duncan address, so Pacific Northwest Raptors and The Raptors are one organisation at one site. The full record lives here; pacific-northwest-raptors.json is a short cross reference only.
No price is published for the school field trip or for the outreach visit to a school. Both pages say only to contact them for pricing and to book. This is the biggest hole in the record.
No minimum or maximum group size is published for the field trip or the outreach visit, and no minimum notice or lead time is given.
No youngest age is stated for a group visit. Children aged 0 to 3 are free on general admission, but nothing says whether a group of under fives is welcomed for the guided field trip.
Washrooms are never mentioned anywhere on the site, including in the questions panel, so nothing was recorded for them.
Nothing is published about what happens in heavy rain. The paths and the demonstration area are outdoors and the only indoor space named is the gift shop.
Bus parking is not addressed. The site says parking is free and that the lot gets busy in summer, which is recorded, but says nothing about a coach.
No email address is published. Contact is by phone or through the message form on the contact page, so no booking email was recorded.
The prices carry no year or season anywhere on the site, so price_year_or_season was left empty. Treat the admission prices as current at the time of checking rather than dated.

The published opening hours stop at 2 November and nothing is shown for winter, so whether the centre opens between November and June is unknown. months_offered is unknown for every program for the same reason.

The questions panel that carries the age rules, the dogs rule, the picnic benches, the parking answer and the Kids Encounter opens as a slide out panel with no page address of its own. Those answers are recorded against the pages the panel opens from.

Summer camps are sold as individual five day registrations for children aged 8 to 12 at $325 with a $100 deposit, not as a group booking, so no program was created for them. The 2026 camp dates published on the site all finished on 21 August 2026.

The image on the field trips section carries the site's own alt text 'Woman holding a golden eagle in front of a group of school children', but the photograph is of a large dark vulture landing on a handler's glove in front of a crowd. The image was opened and looked at, and a written alt was used instead of the site's.
No photograph of the picnic area, the washroom block or the parking lot was found, so there is no space image to show a director the logistics.
The same organisation runs a second, much smaller site called Urban Raptors in Delta near Vancouver, capped at six guests. That is not this venue and nothing from it was recorded here.
The Owl Encounter is marked on the site as currently unavailable and returning in November 2026. It has a minimum age of eight in any case.
